editorial:
Imagine a world where a dying scientist's mind gets uploaded into a supercomputer, and suddenly he has the power to change everything. That's the wild ride you get with this sci-fi thriller. Johnny Depp plays Dr. Will Caster, a brilliant researcher chasing the idea of Technological Singularity, where machines become smarter than humans. After an attack by an anti-tech group leaves him dying, his wife Evelyn and friend Max upload his consciousness into a computer. Soon, Will's digital mind starts growing, building a massive underground lab, and healing people in ways that feel both amazing and scary. The movie has a slow, thoughtful pace that builds tension as you wonder whether this digital Will is still human or something else entirely.

The acting is solid, especially Rebecca Hall as Evelyn, who carries the emotional weight of the story. The visuals are stunning, with beautiful shots of nature mixed with high-tech labs. On the downside, the plot can feel slow and confusing at times, and some ideas never fully pay off. If you enjoy big questions about technology and humanity, you'll find plenty to think about. For the best experience, stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that Will's digital mind was actually trying to heal the planet and connect people, not destroy them. Evelyn realizes too late that the anti-tech group was wrong about him. Will sacrifices himself to save Evelyn, shutting down his network and dying for real. The twist is that Will's nanobots remain in the soil, slowly healing the Earth and bringing back clean water and plants. Max discovers this years later, hinting that Will's dream of a better world quietly lives on.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big questions about technology and humanity.
